Fourteen comments

I first learned this from an old Ceili Band recording (Tulla?), it’s also on Kathleen Collins album in this setting. Matt Molloy recorded a three part setting of this tune on “Molloy, Brady Peoples” (not sure if the title is in that order) which is popular with some flute players but four parts seems to be the more common setting. Fun tune thats got a lot of bounce

↳ Posted by b.maloney on January 25th, 2002.

Re: The Limerick Lasses

Appears in Stephen Grier’s manuscript, book 2, documented by ITMA as The Pretty Little Boy. The manuscript dates from the mid 1800s.

↳ Posted by Petey_Whistle on May 25th, 2020.

The Limerick Lasses, X:7

From the playing of Matt Molloy, Tommy Peoples and Paul Brady - wonderful tune!

↳ Posted by shanachie on August 23rd, 2022.

Re: The Limerick Lasses /Lads

A 2 part version is in O’Neill’s Waifs and Strays of Irish Music (#300) as Limerick Lads. It was from the Rice-Walsh manuscript and therefore from fiddler Jeremiah Breen from Ballyconry, Co Kerry.

↳ Posted by brailsford on January 20th, 2024.

The Limerick Lasses, X:8

This setting is from Alexander’s 50 New Scotch & Irish Reels and Hornpipes, ca. 1825, appearing under the name of “Pretty Girls of Monaghan”.

Source: https://www.village-music-project.org.uk/?page_id=803
